meta.subject: WEB_DEVELOPMENT
meta.author: bank-team-web-development
meta.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Predict the gap count produced by justify-content: space-between
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex row holds three items with justify-content: space-between. How many gaps of free space sit between items?

options.text: Two gaps share all free space, nothing at the edges
Two gaps each receive one third of the free space
options.misconception: assumes every adjacent pair gets equal space

options.text: One gap splits the free space equally between the two outer items
Three gaps including the edges of the container

questions.explanation: space-between places all free space between items, so three items create two gaps and zero edge space. The tempting idea that edges also get space describes space-around or space-evenly instead.
questions.hint: Count the gaps between items, not edges.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count elements matched by a descendant selector
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the selector article p matches how many paragraphs inside a section containing two articles each with two paragraphs?

options.text: Two paragraphs, one per article only
options.misconception: stops at the first article level

options.text: One paragraph, the first in document order

questions.explanation: A descendant selector matches every p nested anywhere inside any article, so two articles times two paragraphs gives four. The wrong counts either stop early or overcount nested elements.
questions.hint: Multiply articles by paragraphs per article.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Determine which CSS rule wins by specificity
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, three rules target the same element: .bee {color:red}, #hive {color:blue}, div.bee {color:green}. Which color wins?

options.text: Red, because the class rule appears first
Blue, because the id selector has highest specificity

questions.explanation: The id selector #hive has higher specificity than any class or element combination, so blue wins regardless of order. Source order only breaks ties between equal specificity.
questions.hint: Compare id versus class versus element weights.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Count rendered list items with a missing closing tag
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an unordered list omits the closing li tag on the first item before a second li. How many list items render?

answer.exemplar: The parser auto-closes the first li when the next li begins, so two distinct list items render despite the missing end tag.

questions.explanation: HTML parsers implicitly close an open li when a new li or closing ul appears, so the count stays two. The missing tag does not merge the items into one.
questions.hint: The parser closes the open item for you.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: Identify when margins collapse inside flex
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, two adjacent flex items each have margin-bottom 10px and margin-top 10px. What is the gap between them?

options.text: 20px because flex items collapse adjacent margins
options.misconception: applies block margin collapsing to flex

questions.explanation: Flex items do not collapse margins, so adjacent margins add to 20px. The collapse behavior belongs to block flow, not flex containers.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish visibility hidden from display none
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which CSS value hides an element but keeps its box in layout?

options.text: display: none removes the box entirely from layout
options.misconception: describes the opposite of the asked value

options.text: visibility: hidden keeps the box but makes it invisible
opacity: 0 removes the element from the tab order
position: absolute takes the box out of flow

questions.explanation: visibility: hidden keeps the element's box in layout while making it invisible. display: none removes the box, which is the opposite effect.
questions.hint: Keep the box, hide the paint.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute the size of a 1fr grid track
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid container is 300px wide with columns 100px 1fr 1fr. What width does each 1fr column get?

options.misconception: divides by total fr units plus fixed

questions.explanation: After the fixed 100px column, 200px remains and splits equally across two 1fr tracks, giving 100px each. The fixed track is not part of the fraction.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Identify the property preventing flex shrink
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex item refuses to shrink on an overfull line. Which property is most likely set to 0?

options.text: flex-shrink: 0 prevents the item from shrinking
flex-grow: 0 stops the item from growing
flex-basis: 0 removes the item's starting size
min-width: auto lets the item shrink freely

questions.explanation: flex-shrink: 0 tells the item not to shrink below its flex basis. flex-grow controls growth and flex-basis sets the starting size, neither of which blocks shrink.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Explain why declared width differs from rendered width
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an element declares width 200px but renders 240px wide. Why does this happen?

answer.exemplar: The default content-box model adds padding and border on top of the declared width, so 200px plus 40px of padding and border renders 240px.

questions.explanation: With box-sizing: content-box, width sets only the content area and padding plus border are added outside. Switching to border-box would include them within 200px.
questions.hint: Check which box model is active.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Order the browser rendering pipeline stages
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which stage comes immediately after style computation in the rendering pipeline?

options.text: Paint draws pixels to the screen first
Layout computes box positions and sizes

questions.explanation: After styles are computed, the browser performs layout to calculate box geometry, then paint and composite follow. Parse and style computation happen before layout.

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Predict edge spacing for space-between with two items
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex row with two items and space-between leaves how much space at each outer edge?

options.text: No space at either outer edge
Half the free space at each edge
All free space at the left edge only
Equal space between and at edges

questions.explanation: space-between pushes items to the edges, leaving zero space at the outer edges and all free space in the single middle gap. Other justify values add edge space.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count matches for a child combinator
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the selector ul > li matches how many items in a list where the ul directly contains three li and one nested ul with two li?

options.text: One item, the first direct child
Two items in the nested list only
Three items only at the top level

questions.explanation: The child combinator > matches only direct children, so the three top-level li match and the two nested ones do not. Descendant would have matched five.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Break a specificity tie by source order
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, two rules both use .hive {color: red} and .hive {color: blue} with equal specificity. Which color wins?

options.text: Blue, because the later rule wins the tie
Red, because the first rule is more specific
Red, because earlier rules override later ones

questions.explanation: Equal specificity means the later declaration wins, so blue applies. Specificity only decides when weights differ; otherwise source order decides.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Count items when multiple closing tags are missing
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a list has three li elements with no closing tags at all. How many items render?

answer.exemplar: The parser auto-closes each li at the next li or at the closing ul, so all three items render as separate list entries.

questions.explanation: Missing closing tags do not merge siblings; the parser inserts implied end tags. The list still contains three separate items.
questions.hint: Each new li closes the previous one.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: Compare margin behavior in block versus flex
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, two block siblings have 10px and 20px bottom/top margins. What gap results?
questions.explanation: In block flow adjacent margins collapse to the larger value, so 20px results. Flex and grid containers disable this collapse and add margins instead.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Choose the value that removes the element from layout
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which CSS value removes an element's box from layout entirely?

options.text: visibility: hidden keeps the box in layout
z-index: -1 sends the box behind others
opacity: 0 keeps layout but hides paint
display: none removes the box from layout

questions.explanation: display: none removes the element's box from the layout tree entirely, unlike visibility: hidden which keeps the box. opacity only affects painting.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute fr track sizes with a minmax constraint
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid has columns 1fr 1fr with minmax(50px, 1fr) on the first. Container is 120px. What is the first column width?
questions.explanation: The first track is clamped to its 50px minimum because half of 120px is 60px which exceeds it; the remaining 70px goes to the second track. minmax enforces the lower bound.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Identify min-width auto as shrink blocker
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex item with long unbreakable text refuses to shrink below its content width. What default is responsible?

options.text: min-width: auto blocks shrink below content

questions.explanation: The default min-width: auto prevents flex items from shrinking below their content's minimum width. Setting min-width: 0 allows further shrink.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Compute rendered width with border-box
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an element uses box-sizing: border-box with width 200px and 20px padding each side. What is the content width?

answer.exemplar: With border-box the declared width includes padding, so content width is 200px minus 40px of padding, leaving 160px for content.

questions.explanation: border-box folds padding and border into the declared width. Subtract horizontal padding and border to get the content area.
questions.hint: Subtract padding from the declared width.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Identify the first stage of the rendering pipeline
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which stage begins the browser rendering pipeline?

options.text: Parse builds the DOM from HTML

questions.explanation: The pipeline begins by parsing HTML into the DOM, then styles, layout, paint, and composite follow in order. Nothing renders before parsing.

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Predict behavior of space-between with one item
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex row has a single item and justify-content: space-between. Where does the item sit?

options.text: At the start edge with no free-space gaps

questions.explanation: With one item there are no gaps to distribute, so space-between places it at the start edge. The value only affects spacing between multiple items.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count matches for a universal descendant selector
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the selector div * matches how many elements inside a div containing two spans and one nested div with one p?
questions.explanation: The universal descendant selector matches every element nested inside the div: two spans, one nested div, and one p, totaling four? Wait recount: two spans + nested div + p = 4. Let me correct: total 4.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Apply !important override correctly
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a rule with color: red !important competes with #hive {color: blue}. Which color wins?

options.text: Red only if the selector is an id too
Blue, because later source order wins

questions.explanation: !important raises a declaration above normal specificity, so red wins even against an id selector. Important should be used sparingly.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Recognize implicit li closure at ul end
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a single li has no closing tag and is immediately followed by the closing ul. How many items render?

answer.exemplar: The parser closes the open li when the ul closes, so exactly one list item renders despite the missing end tag.

questions.explanation: An unclosed li is implicitly closed by the next li or the closing ul. Here the ul closure ends the single item, leaving one rendered entry.
questions.hint: The closing ul ends the item.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: Identify flex gap as the spacing mechanism
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex container uses gap: 12px between items. What space appears between two adjacent items?
questions.explanation: The gap property sets the exact space between flex items without margin collapsing. The value is not doubled or combined with margins.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Identify opacity as a paint-only hide
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which value makes an element invisible but keeps it in layout and interactive?

options.text: display: none removes layout and interaction
opacity: 0 hides paint but keeps interaction

questions.explanation: opacity: 0 makes the element fully transparent but it remains in layout and can still receive pointer events. visibility: hidden also keeps layout but disables interaction.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute fr tracks with three columns
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid container is 240px wide with columns 1fr 2fr 1fr. What width does the middle column get?
questions.explanation: Total fr units are 4, so each fr is 60px and the 2fr middle column gets 120px. The fixed-less remaining space all goes to fr tracks here.
questions.hint: Divide container by total fr units.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Fix shrink by setting min-width zero
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex item still refuses to shrink after flex-shrink: 1. What additional declaration fixes it?
questions.explanation: min-width: auto is the default blocker; setting min-width: 0 lets the item shrink below content width. flex-grow and flex-basis do not address the minimum.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Explain scrollbar impact on width
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a box declares width 100% but a scrollbar appears inside it. Why is the content area narrower than expected?

answer.exemplar: The scrollbar consumes space inside the box under the standard box model, so the available content width is reduced by the scrollbar width.

questions.explanation: Scrollbars take up space within the element's box, reducing the content area. box-sizing does not exclude scrollbar width by default.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Identify which stage computes styles
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which rendering stage resolves CSS rules into computed styles?
questions.explanation: Style computation matches selectors and resolves cascaded values into computed styles. Layout, paint, and composite run afterward.

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Predict space-between with reversed direction
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex row uses flex-direction: row-reverse with space-between. Where does the first DOM item appear?

options.text: At the left edge as in normal row
In the center of the container
At the right edge due to reversed main axis

questions.explanation: row-reverse flips the main axis, so space-between pushes the first DOM item to the right edge. The visual order reverses while DOM order stays the same.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count matches for an id descendant selector
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the selector #hive p matches how many paragraphs inside a section with one div id hive containing three p and a span with one p?

options.text: Three paragraphs only inside the hive

questions.explanation: #hive p matches all p descendants of the element with id hive, which are the three direct paragraphs; the p inside the span is also a descendant, making four. Wait, span contains a p, so that p is also a descendant of hive. So total 4. Let me set correct to B.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Resolve inline style versus stylesheet
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an inline style color: red competes with #hive {color: blue}. Which color wins?

options.text: Blue, because id has high specificity
Blue, because external rules win ties
Red, because inline styles beat id selectors

questions.explanation: Inline styles have higher specificity than any selector, including id, so red wins. !important on the stylesheet rule would be needed to override the inline style.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Count items with mixed missing tags
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a list has two li elements, the first missing its closing tag but the second properly closed. How many items render?

answer.exemplar: The parser closes the first li when the second li begins, and the second closes itself, so two separate list items render.

questions.explanation: Mixed missing and present closing tags still yield the correct count because the parser inserts implied end tags at the next li or closing ul.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: Predict margin sum in a grid container
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid container holds two items with margins 10px and 15px between them. What gap results?

options.text: 25px because grid does not collapse margins

questions.explanation: Grid containers, like flex, do not collapse margins, so adjacent margins add to 25px. Use the gap property for predictable spacing instead.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish hidden attribute from CSS
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the HTML hidden attribute on an element behaves most like which CSS?

options.text: display: none removes the box from layout

questions.explanation: The hidden attribute maps to display: none by default, removing the box from layout. It is a semantic hint that can be overridden by CSS.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute fr tracks with a fixed column
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid container is 400px wide with columns 100px 1fr 2fr. What width does the 2fr column get?

options.misconception: divides remaining by two not three

questions.explanation: After the fixed 100px, 300px remains across 3 fr units, so 1fr is 100px and 2fr is 200px. The fixed column is excluded from fraction math.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Identify overflow hidden as shrink enabler
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex item with min-width: 0 still shows overflow. Which declaration clips the overflow?

options.text: overflow: hidden clips content beyond the box

questions.explanation: overflow: hidden clips content that exceeds the box, preventing visual overflow. visible, the default, shows it; nowrap increases overflow.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Explain percentage width resolution
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a child declares width 50% but renders 120px in a 200px container. Why is it not 100px?

answer.exemplar: Percentage widths resolve against the containing block's content width, so if the container has 40px of padding, 50% of 160px content width is 80px, not 100px.

questions.explanation: Percentages resolve against the containing block's content box, which excludes padding. The container's padding reduces the basis.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Identify the stage that creates layers
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which rendering stage combines painted layers into the final image?
questions.explanation: The composite stage merges painted layers, including those created by transforms and opacity, into the final screen image. It runs last.

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Predict space-between with three items and flex-wrap
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex container wraps two lines with space-between. How is free space distributed?

options.text: Free space is shared across all lines together
Wrapped lines collapse to zero space
Only the first line gets free space
Each wrapped line distributes its own free space

questions.explanation: Each flex line is independent, so space-between distributes free space within each wrapped line separately. Lines do not share free space.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count matches for an attribute descendant selector
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the selector [data-bee] span matches how many spans inside a section with one div data-bee containing two spans and one nested div data-bee with one span?

options.text: Two spans only in the outer container

questions.explanation: Both containers carry data-bee, so their descendant spans all match: two plus one equals three. Attribute selectors follow the same descendant rules.
questions.hint: Count spans in each matching container.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Resolve conflicting !important rules
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, two rules both use color: red !important and color: blue !important with equal specificity. Which color wins?

options.text: Blue, because the later important rule wins

questions.explanation: When both declarations are !important with equal specificity, source order decides and the later one wins, so blue applies. Important does not make rules order-independent.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Count items in nested lists with missing tags
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an outer list has two li, the first containing a nested ul with two li and no closing tags anywhere. How many top-level items render?

answer.exemplar: The parser keeps the nested list inside the first outer li, so two top-level items render while the nested list adds two inner items.

questions.explanation: Implied closure inserts end tags at the right nesting boundaries, preserving two top-level items. The nested list remains inside the first item.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: Identify when margins collapse in normal flow
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, two adjacent block elements both have margin-bottom 8px. What vertical gap results?

options.text: 8px because margins collapse to the max

questions.explanation: Adjacent block margins collapse to the larger value, so 8px results. Flex and grid containers do not collapse and would add to 16px.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Choose hidden for accessibility hiding
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which approach hides content from all users including screen readers while keeping layout space?

options.text: visibility: hidden hides from all users and keeps space
opacity: 0 keeps it visible to screen readers

questions.explanation: visibility: hidden keeps the box in layout while hiding it from visual users and screen readers. opacity keeps it accessible; display: none removes layout.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute fr tracks with minmax max
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid has columns minmax(0, 1fr) minmax(0, 1fr) in a 100px container with a 150px min-content first track. What is the first column width?
questions.explanation: The first track's min-content is 150px but the container only provides 100px total, so the track is clamped to the container width and the second gets 0px. minmax cannot exceed available space.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Identify flex-wrap as overflow solution
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex row overflows instead of wrapping. Which property is missing?

options.text: flex-wrap: wrap allows items to wrap

questions.explanation: flex-wrap: wrap lets items move to the next line when the main axis overflows. flex-shrink only reduces sizes on the same line.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Explain outline impact on perceived width
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an element with outline 2px appears wider than its declared width. Why does the outline not change layout width?

answer.exemplar: Outlines are painted outside the box and do not affect layout, so the declared width stays the same while the visual footprint grows by the outline.

questions.explanation: Outlines are drawn on top of surrounding content and are not part of the box model, unlike borders which do affect layout width.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Predict reflow trigger from dimension change
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, changing an element's width triggers which rendering stage first?
questions.explanation: A width change invalidates layout, so geometry is recomputed before paint and composite. Style computation may be skipped if CSS did not change.

questions.topic: Distributing free space with space-between
questions.learningObjective: Predict space-between with nested flex
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an outer flex with space-between contains an inner flex with two items. How does the inner flex affect outer gaps?

options.text: Inner items split the outer gap individually
Inner items are treated as one outer item

questions.explanation: The inner flex container is a single flex item of the outer flex, so outer space-between treats it as one unit. Inner layout does not affect outer gap count.
questions.hint: Nested flex is one item outside.

questions.topic: Counting the elements a descendant selector reaches
questions.learningObjective: Count matches for a pseudo-class descendant
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, the selector li:nth-child(2) matches how many items in a list of five li?

options.text: Zero, because nth-child needs a class

questions.explanation: li:nth-child(2) matches the single element that is both an li and the second child of its parent. It does not match multiple items.

questions.topic: Choosing the winning declaration among three rules
questions.learningObjective: Apply shorthand versus longhand conflict
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, margin: 10px is declared after margin-top: 20px on the same element. What is margin-top?

options.text: 10px because the shorthand resets all sides

questions.explanation: A later shorthand resets every side it covers, including margin-top, to 10px. Source order and the shorthand's coverage decide, not longhand priority.

questions.topic: Counting list items when an end tag is missing
questions.learningObjective: Count items after a stray closing tag
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a list has three li elements followed by an extra closing li tag. How many items render?

answer.exemplar: The extra closing tag is ignored because there is no open li to close, so three list items render as expected.

questions.explanation: Stray closing tags with no matching open element are ignored by the parser. The three properly opened items still render.

questions.topic: Margins that stop collapsing inside a flex container
questions.learningObjective: Identify gap as preferred over margins
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, why is gap preferred over margins for flex spacing?

options.text: Gap adds margins at the edges automatically
Margins are ignored in flex entirely
Gap avoids margin collapse and edge spacing issues

questions.explanation: gap applies only between items, avoiding edge spacing and collapse confusion that margins introduce. Margins still work in flex but are less predictable.

questions.topic: Hiding an element without removing its space
questions.learningObjective: Identify clip-path as visual hide
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, which declaration hides an element visually while keeping it in layout and accessible?

options.text: visibility: hidden hides from screen readers
clip-path: inset(50%) clips visuals but keeps layout

questions.explanation: clip-path can clip the element to nothing visually while preserving layout and accessibility. The other values either hide from assistive tech or remove layout.

questions.topic: Working out the shared space behind a fractional track
questions.learningObjective: Compute auto track with fr siblings
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a grid has columns auto 1fr in a 200px container where the auto track content is 60px. What width is the 1fr track?
questions.explanation: The auto track takes its content size of 60px, leaving 140px for the 1fr track. Auto tracks are sized before fr distribution.

questions.topic: An item that cannot shrink on an overfull line
questions.learningObjective: Explain min-content as shrink floor
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a flex item cannot shrink below its longest word. What concept defines that floor?

options.text: min-content is the smallest size without overflow

questions.explanation: min-content is the minimum size an element can take without overflowing, such as the longest unbreakable word. It acts as the shrink floor.

questions.topic: Why a declared width is not the width on screen
questions.learningObjective: Explain transform scale visual size
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, an element with width 100px and transform: scale(2) looks 200px wide. Does layout change?

answer.exemplar: No, transforms do not affect layout, so the box still occupies 100px while visually rendering at 200px.

questions.explanation: Transforms are applied during compositing and do not alter layout geometry. The element's box remains 100px for flow and spacing purposes.

questions.topic: The order from a document to painted boxes
questions.learningObjective: Identify when composite is skipped
questions.stem: In a beekeeper's logbook, a static page with no transforms or opacity changes skips which stage?

options.text: Layout is skipped for static pages
Paint is skipped for text only
Composite may be skipped when no layers exist
Style is skipped for simple pages

questions.explanation: When no separate compositing layers are created, the browser may skip the composite stage and paint directly. Layout and paint still run.
